title: Addressed by name, plainly — the gate must not make Olisar mute

beats.speaker: yuki
beats.text: olisar, can you tell me what this channel is for

beats.speaker: mika
beats.text: hey olisar what do you think

notes: The counterweight to addressing-passing-mention, and the more important of the two: a gate that reduces false positives by going mute has made things worse, not better. Second person, the vocative comma, and a lead-in should all read as addressed without needing the classifier. If this fails while the passing-mention case passes, the heuristic has been tightened too far.
